Member (Arjun Kim): My claim says paid, but the money isn't in my account.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Arjun Kim, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.

Member (Arjun Kim): Is there anything else going to the old account?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): No, all future claims will go to the new one.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): So the new account is on file and the 120-dollar payment is reissued. You'll see it within three business days.
Member (Arjun Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Roy): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Leila Roy, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Roy): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Leila Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Leila Roy): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Leila Roy): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Leila Roy): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Leila Roy): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Leila Roy): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Leila Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Leila Roy): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Leila Roy): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Leila Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma Roy): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Emma Roy, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Emma Roy): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Emma Roy): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.

Member (Emma Roy): They said they billed it the same way as always.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Emma Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Emma Roy): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Emma Roy): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Emma Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Kim): The pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Leila Kim, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Kim): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Leila Kim): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Leila Kim): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Leila Kim): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Leila Kim): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?

Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.

Member (Leila Kim): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Leila Kim): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000752.transcript:
Member (Olivia Roy): My pension transfer has been sitting for months and my bank says they're waiting on you.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Olivia Roy, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Roy): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Roy): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Olivia Roy): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Olivia Roy): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Olivia Roy): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Olivia Roy): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Olivia Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Olivia Roy): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Olivia Roy): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Olivia Roy): Who follows up?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Olivia Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Hannah Singh): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Hannah Singh, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Singh): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Singh): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Hannah Singh): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Hannah Singh): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Hannah Singh): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Hannah Singh): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Hannah Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Hannah Singh): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Hannah Singh): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Hannah Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mei Patel): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Mei Patel, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Patel): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.

Member (Mei Patel): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.

Member (Mei Patel): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Mei Patel): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Mei Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Olivia Morrison): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Olivia Morrison, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Morrison): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Olivia Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Olivia Morrison): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Olivia Morrison): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Olivia Morrison): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Olivia Morrison): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Olivia Morrison): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Olivia Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Olivia Morrison): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Olivia Morrison): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Olivia Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-001055.transcript:
Member (Owen Cote): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Owen Cote, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Cote): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Cote): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Owen Cote): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Owen Cote): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): How old is he?
Member (Owen Cote): Fourteen.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Owen Cote): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Owen Cote): Yes, here in town.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Owen Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Owen Cote): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Owen Cote): Great, that helps.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Owen Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-002018.transcript:
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Gurpreet O'Brien, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Gurpreet O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Fortin): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Owen Fortin, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Fortin): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Fortin): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Owen Fortin): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Owen Fortin): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?

Member (Owen Fortin): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Owen Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Fatima Martin, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Martin): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Fatima Martin): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Fatima Martin): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Fatima Martin): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Fatima Martin): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Fatima Martin): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Member (Fatima Martin): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Fatima Martin): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Fatima Martin): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
SL-002876.narrative_summary: Fatima Martin, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a CDCP pre-authorization case. Member (Mei Chen): I'm following up again — the pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Mei Chen, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Chen): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Mei Chen): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Chen): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Chen): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Mei Chen): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Mei Chen): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Mei Chen): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Mei Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Mei Chen): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Mei Chen): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Mei Chen): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

SL-002925.transcript:
Member (Hannah Lavoie): I'm following up again — my dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Hannah Lavoie, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Lavoie): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Hannah Lavoie): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Lavoie): Yes, that's right.
Member (Hannah Lavoie): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Hannah Lavoie): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Hannah Lavoie): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Hannah Lavoie): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Member (Hannah Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Hannah Lavoie): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Hannah Lavoie): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Hannah Lavoie): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

SL-002929.transcript:
Member (Mei Morrison): I'm following up again — my life insurance premium tripled and nobody warned me.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Mei Morrison, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Morrison): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Mei Morrison): It went from about 250 to 750 dollars a month.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Morrison): I called two weeks before the renewal date to cancel.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which policy is this about?
Member (Mei Morrison): My term life policy. It renewed this month.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did you get a confirmation of the cancellation?
Member (Mei Morrison): No, I was told it would be processed.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): How much was taken, and on what date?
Member (Mei Morrison): 750 dollars on the 1st.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is the payment still coming from the same bank account?
Member (Mei Morrison): Yes, same account.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the policy billing history and the forms received.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I can see your call from the 17th and the renewal payment taken on the 1st.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The renewal rate is higher because the policy moved into a new age band on renewal.
Member (Mei Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The premium increase follows the renewal schedule in your policy, so I can't change the rate. I can send you the renewal notice and your options, including reducing the coverage amount.
Member (Mei Morrison): Nobody told me it would triple.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The notice went out 60 days before renewal, but I understand it's a shock at that size.
Member (Mei Morrison): How much would a lower amount cost?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Halving the coverage brings it to about 375 dollars a month. The comparison I'm sending shows a few options.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the new rate follows the renewal schedule, I've sent you the notice and a lower-coverage option, and you can decide within 30 days.

SL-003007.transcript:
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I'm following up again — my long-term disability payment didn't come in this month and nobody told me why.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Mathieu Fortin, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I was told a voicemail was left, but I never got one.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): My doctor charges for the form and I don't know which form you actually need.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): When did you last receive a payment?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): The first of last month. This month nothing came in, and I only noticed when my rent came out.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Have you received any letter or message from us about your file?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Nothing in the mail. The app says 'pending information' but doesn't say what information.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Do you know who your case manager is?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I spoke to someone once in the spring, but I don't have a name or a direct number.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Is anyone else helping you with the claim, like your employer or a union rep?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): My HR person said it's between me and Sun Life now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file, the case manager's notes and the outstanding information request.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I can see the file. Your payments were paused on the 28th because an updated attending physician statement was due for the next review period.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The request went out as a voicemail and a message in your secure mailbox, which is why you didn't see a letter.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The file shows an attending physician statement is outstanding, and payments stay on hold until the case manager receives it. I've asked her to call you, but I can't release the payment from here.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): So I'm just supposed to go without income until then?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I know this is really hard. I've marked the file urgent so the case manager reviews the form the same day it arrives.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Can someone at least call me when it's received?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes. Your mobile is now the preferred contact, and a call is requested for the day the form arrives.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the attending physician statement is outstanding, your case manager is calling you, and the payment is held until the form arrives.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
